13: class GNCLClassifier(Ensemble):
14:     """(Generalized) Negative Correlation Learning.
15: 
16:     Negative Correlation Learning uses the Bias-Variance-Co-Variance decomposition to derive a regularized objective function which enforces diversity among the ensemble members. The first appearance of this work was for the MSE loss in [1,2]. A modern application to the problem of crowd counting can be found in [4]. Optiz later proposed a similar objective using the Cross Entropy Loss, but without theoretical justifications [3]. Webb et al. in [5,6] gave more theoretical background for using the Cross Entropy Loss. Note that [6] is basically a shorter version of [5].
17: 
18:     We generalized and unified the previous works to include _any_ loss function using a second order Taylor approximation. As detailed in our paper, there is an upper bound for the GNCL objective which does not compute the exact diversity term. Thus, any differentiable loss \( \ell \) function can be used for optimization. We will refer to this mode as `upper`. Let \( f(x) \) be the ensembles prediction consisting of M models \( \{h^1, \dots, h^M\} \), then 
19: 
20:     $$
21:         \\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^N \lambda \ell(f(x_j),y_j) + \\frac{1-\lambda}{M}\sum_{i=1}^M \ell(h^i(x_j),y_j)
22:     $$
23: 
24:     where \( \lambda \in [0,1] \) is the trade-off between the ensemble's performance and its diversity.
25: 
26:     If you are interested in explicitly computing the diversity we currently supports three loss functions: MSE, Negative Log-Likelihood and CrossEntropy. We call this mode `exact`. In this case the following objective is used:
27:     $$
28:         \\frac{1}{M} \sum_{i=1}^M \ell(h^i) - \\frac{\lambda}{2M} \sum_{i=1}^M {d_i}^T D d_i
29:     $$
30:     where \( D = \\nabla^2_{f(x)}\ell(f(x), y), d_i = (h^i(x) - f(x))\) is optimized.
31: 
32:     Note that PyTorchs autograd functionality does not directly support a hessian (or even gradients) on a "per example" basis, but only summed over a batch. So far I have not found a way to use autograd efficiently here. Therefore, this mode is currently restricted to the three mentioned loss functions.
33:                 
34:     Attributes:
35:         n_estimators (int): Number of estimators in ensemble. Should be at least 1
36:         
37:         l_reg (float): Trade-off between diversity and loss. Should be between 0 and 1. l_reg = 0 implies independent training whereas l_reg = 1 implies no independent training
38: 
39:         mode (str): The mode used for fitting a new model. 
40:             
41:             - `mode != "exact"`: The upper bound is used for fitting. 
42:             - `mode == "exact"`: The diversity is explicity computed and used for fitting. Only `nn.MSELoss`, `nn.NLLLoss`, `nn.CrossEntropyLoss` are supported.
43: 
44:     __References__
45: 
46:     [1] Liu, Y., & Yao, X. (1999). Ensemble learning via negative correlation. Neural Networks, 12(10), 1399–1404. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0893-6080(99)00073-8 
47: 
48:     [2] Brown, G., WatT, J. L., & Tino, P. (2005). Managing Diversity in Regression Ensembles. Jmlr, (6), 1621–1650. https://doi.org/10.1097/IYC.0000000000000008
49: 
50:     [3] Opitz, M., Possegger, H., & Bischof, H. (2016). Efficient model averaging for deep neural networks. Asian Conference on Computer Vision, 10112 LNCS, 205–220. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-54184-6_13
51: 
52:     [4] Shi, Z., Zhang, L., Liu, Y., Cao, X., Ye, Y., Cheng, M., & Zheng, G. (n.d.). Crowd Counting with Deep Negative Correlation Learning, 5382–5390. Retrieved from http://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_cvpr_2018/papers/Shi_Crowd_Counting_With_CVPR_2018_paper.pdf
53: 
54:     [5] Webb, A. M., Reynolds, C., Iliescu, D.-A., Reeve, H., Lujan, M., & Brown, G. (2019). Joint Training of Neural Network Ensembles, (4), 1–14. https://doi.org/10.13140/RG.2.2.28091.46880
55: 
56:     [6] Webb, A. M., Reynolds, C., Chen, W., Reeve, H., Iliescu, D.-A., Lujan, M., & Brown, G. (2020). To Ensemble or Not Ensemble: When does End-To-End Training Fail? In ECML PKDD 2020 (pp. 1–16). Retrieved from http://www.cs.man.ac.uk/~gbrown/publications/ecml2020webb.pdf
57: """
58: 
59:     def __init__(self, l_reg = 0, mode = "exact", *args, **kwargs):
60:         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
61:         self.l_reg = l_reg
62:         self.mode = mode
63:         self.estimators_ = nn.ModuleList([ self.base_estimator() for _ in range(self.n_estimators)])
64: 
65:         if self.mode == "exact" and not isinstance(self.loss_function, (nn.MSELoss, nn.NLLLoss, nn.CrossEntropyLoss)):
66:             warnings.warn("You set GNCL to 'exact' but used an unsupported loss function for exact minimization. Currrently supported are MSELoss, NLLLoss, and CrossEntropyLoss. I am setting mode to 'upper' now and minimize the upper bound using the provided loss function") 
67:             self.mode = "upper"
68: 
69:     def restore_state(self, checkpoint):
70:         super().restore_state(checkpoint)
71:         self.mode = checkpoint["mode"]
72: 
73:     def get_state(self):
74:         state = super().get_state()
75:         return {
76:             **state,
77:             "mode":self.mode,
78:         } 
79: 
80:     def prepare_backward(self, data, target, weights = None):
81:         # TODO Make use of the weights as well!
82:         f_bar, base_preds = self.forward_with_base(data)
83:         
84:         if self.mode == "upper":
85:             n_classes = f_bar.shape[1]
86:             n_preds = f_bar.shape[0]
87:             D = torch.eye(n_classes).repeat(n_preds, 1, 1).cuda()
88:         else:
89:             if isinstance(self.loss_function, nn.MSELoss): 
90:                 n_classes = f_bar.shape[1]
91:                 n_preds = f_bar.shape[0]
92: 
93:                 eye_matrix = torch.eye(n_classes).repeat(n_preds, 1, 1).cuda()
94:                 D = 2.0*eye_matrix
95:             elif isinstance(self.loss_function, nn.NLLLoss):
96:                 n_classes = f_bar.shape[1]
97:                 n_preds = f_bar.shape[0]
98:                 D = torch.eye(n_classes).repeat(n_preds, 1, 1).cuda()
99:                 target_one_hot = torch.nn.functional.one_hot(target, num_classes = n_classes).type(self.get_float_type())
100: 
101:                 eps = 1e-7
102:                 diag_vector = target_one_hot*(1.0/(f_bar**2+eps))
103:                 D.diagonal(dim1=-2, dim2=-1).copy_(diag_vector)
104:             elif isinstance(self.loss_function, nn.CrossEntropyLoss):
105:                 n_preds = f_bar.shape[0]
106:                 n_classes = f_bar.shape[1]
107:                 f_bar_softmax = nn.functional.softmax(f_bar,dim=1)
108:                 D = -1.0*torch.bmm(f_bar_softmax.unsqueeze(2), f_bar_softmax.unsqueeze(1))
109:                 diag_vector = f_bar_softmax*(1.0-f_bar_softmax)
110:                 D.diagonal(dim1=-2, dim2=-1).copy_(diag_vector)
111:             else:
112:                 # NOTE: We should never reach this code path
113:                 raise ValueError("Invalid combination of mode and loss function in GNCLClassifier.")
114: 
115:         losses = []
116:         accuracies = []
117:         diversity = []
118:         f_loss = self.loss_function(f_bar, target)
119:         for pred in base_preds:
120:             diff = pred - f_bar 
121:             covar = torch.bmm(diff.unsqueeze(1), torch.bmm(D, diff.unsqueeze(2))).squeeze()
122:             div = 1.0/self.n_estimators * 1.0/2.0 * covar
123:             i_loss = self.loss_function(pred, target)
124: 
125:             if self.mode == "exact":
126:                 # Eq. (4)
127:                 reg_loss = 1.0/self.n_estimators * i_loss - self.l_reg * div
128:             else:
129:                 # Eq. (5) where we scale the ensemble loss with 1.0/self.n_estimators due to the summation in line 118
130:                 reg_loss = 1.0/self.n_estimators * self.l_reg * f_loss + (1.0 - self.l_reg)/self.n_estimators * i_loss
131:             
132:             losses.append(reg_loss)
133:             accuracies.append(100.0*(pred.argmax(1) == target).type(self.get_float_type()))
134:             diversity.append(div)
135: 
136:         losses = torch.stack(losses, dim = 1)
137:         accuracies = torch.stack(accuracies, dim = 1)
138:         diversity = torch.stack(diversity, dim = 1)
139:         
140:         # NOTE: avg loss is the average (regularized) loss and not the average loss (wrt. to the loss_function)
141:         d = {
142:             "prediction" : f_bar, 
143:             "backward" : losses.sum(dim=1), 
144:             "metrics" :
145:             {
146:                 "loss" : f_loss,
147:                 "accuracy" : 100.0*(f_bar.argmax(1) == target).type(self.get_float_type()), 
148:                 "avg loss": losses.mean(dim=1),
149:                 "avg accuracy": accuracies.mean(dim = 1),
150:                 "diversity": diversity.sum(dim = 1)
151:             } 
152:             
153:         }
154:         return d

22: class E2EEnsembleClassifier(Ensemble):
23:     """ End-to-End (E2E) Learning of the entire ensemble by viewing it as a single model.
24:     
25:     Directly E2E training of the entire ensemble. Just get the prediction of each base model, aggregate it and perform SGD on it as if it would be a new fancy Deep Learning architecture. Surprisingly, this approach is often overlooked in literature and sometimes it has strange names. I'll try to gather some references below, but apart from that there is nothing out of the ordinary to explain about this model compared to regular Deep architectures. 
26: 
27:     __References__
28:     
29:     [1] Dutt, A., Pellerin, D., & Quénot, G. (2020). Coupled ensembles of neural networks. Neurocomputing, 396, 346–357. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2018.10.092
30: 
31:     [2] Lee, S., Purushwalkam, S., Cogswell, M., Crandall, D., & Batra, D. (2015). Why M Heads are Better than One: Training a Diverse Ensemble of Deep Networks. Retrieved from http://arxiv.org/abs/1511.06314
32:     
33:     [3] Webb, A. M., Reynolds, C., Iliescu, D.-A., Reeve, H., Lujan, M., & Brown, G. (2019). Joint Training of Neural Network Ensembles, (4), 1–14. https://doi.org/10.13140/RG.2.2.28091.46880
34:     
35:     [4] Webb, A. M., Reynolds, C., Chen, W., Reeve, H., Iliescu, D.-A., Lujan, M., & Brown, G. (2020). To Ensemble or Not Ensemble: When does End-To-End Training Fail? In ECML PKDD 2020 (pp. 1–16). Retrieved from http://www.cs.man.ac.uk/~gbrown/publications/ecml2020webb.pdf
36:     """
37:     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
38:         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
39:         self.estimators_ = nn.ModuleList([ self.base_estimator() for _ in range(self.n_estimators)])
40: 
41:     def prepare_backward(self, data, target, weights = None):
42:         f_bar, base_preds = self.forward_with_base(data)
43:         loss = self.loss_function(f_bar, target)
44: 
45:         if weights is not None:
46:             loss = loss * weights
47: 
48:         accuracies = []
49:         losses = []
50:         for pred in base_preds:
51:             iloss = self.loss_function(pred, target)
52:             if weights is not None:
53:                 iloss *= weights 
54:             losses.append(iloss.detach())
55:             accuracies.append(100.0*(pred.argmax(1) == target).type(self.get_float_type()))
56: 
57:         avg_losses = torch.stack(losses, dim = 1).mean(dim = 1)
58:         avg_accuracy = torch.stack(accuracies, dim = 1).mean(dim = 1)
59: 
60:         d = {
61:             "prediction" : f_bar, 
62:             "backward" : loss, 
63:             "metrics" :
64:             {
65:                 "loss" : loss.detach(),
66:                 "accuracy" : 100.0*(f_bar.argmax(1) == target).type(self.get_float_type()), 
67:                 "avg loss": avg_losses,
68:                 "avg accuracy": avg_accuracy
69:             } 
70:             
71:         }
72:         return d

470: class Ensemble(BaseModel):
471:     """ Ensemble
472: 
473:     This is an extension of the BaseModel specifically for ensembles. This class offers a `forward_with_base` function which returns all individual predictions as well as the combined predictions. 
474: 
475:     Attributes:
476: 
477:         combination_type (str, optional): The way individual predictions are combined. Defaults to `average`. Available are:
478: 
479:             -  `average`: Uses $$ f(x) = \\frac{1}{M} \sum_{i=1}^M h^i(x) $$
480:             -  `softmax`: Applies the softmax function to the average $$ f(x) = softmax(\\frac{1}{M} \sum_{i=1}^M h^i(x)) $$
481:             -  `best`: Returns the most confident prediction across all models,  $$ f(x) = \arg\max_{i=1,\dots,M, j=1,\dots,C} \{h^i(x)_j\}$$
482:         
483:         n_estimators (int, optional): The number of estimators in the ensemble. Defaults to 5. Should be at-least 1.
484:     """
485: 
486:     def __init__(self, n_estimators = 5, combination_type = "average", *args, **kwargs):
487:         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
488:         self.combination_type = combination_type
489:         self.n_estimators = n_estimators
490:         
491:         assert self.n_estimators > 0, "Your ensemble should have at-least one member, but self.n_estimators was {}".format(self.n_estimators)
492:         assert self.combination_type  in ('average', 'softmax', 'best'), "Combination type must be one of ('average', 'softmax', 'best')"
493: 
494:     def restore_state(self, checkpoint):
495:         super().restore_state(checkpoint)
496:         self.combination_type = checkpoint["combination_type"]
497:         self.n_estimators = checkpoint["n_estimators"]
498: 
499:     def get_state(self):
500:         state = super().get_state()
501:         return {
502:             **state,
503:             "combination_type":self.combination_type,
504:             "n_estimators":self.n_estimators
505:         }
506: 
507:     def forward(self, X):
508:         return self.forward_with_base(X)[0]
509: 
510:     # @torch.jit.script
511:     def forward_with_base(self, X):
512:         base_preds = [e(X) for e in self.estimators_] #self.n_estimators
513:         # Some ensemble methods may introduce / remove new models while optimization. Thus we cannot use
514:         # self.n_estimators which is the (maximum) number of models in the ensemble, but not the current one
515:         n_estimators = len(self.estimators_)
516:         if self.combination_type == "average":
517:             pred_combined = 1.0/n_estimators*torch.sum(torch.stack(base_preds, dim=1),dim=1)
518:         elif self.combination_type == "softmax":
519:             pred_combined = 1.0/n_estimators*torch.sum(torch.stack(base_preds, dim=1),dim=1)
520:             pred_combined = nn.functional.softmax(pred_combined,dim=1)
521:         else:   
522:             pred_combined, _ = torch.stack(base_preds, dim=1).max(dim=1)
523:         
524:         return pred_combined, base_preds
